label: MODEL_ONLY FORECAST_ONLY NOT_MEASURED_IN_THIS_SYSTEM
owner: STACK.md (narrative) + this file (machine-readable); code is the authority and both mirror it

adoption_levels.ADOPTED: in use, exercised by CI or the workflow, and its behaviour is verified in this repository
adoption_levels.STAGED: interface and acceptance criteria are written and executable, but the tool is not installed, not exercised, and produces nothing authoritative
adoption_levels.DEFERRED: deliberately not built; the contract is recorded so later work is implementation rather than redesign
adoption_levels.ADOPTED_ADMISSION_MECHANISM_ONLY: the governing rule or gate is in use and verified, but the tool it governs is not consumed by any scientific path
adoption_levels.RESOLVED: decided by a measured rule: each candidate explicitly adopted or rejected, the decision committed and re-derived on a hosted runner; nothing is in force beyond what the decision says

invariants: additive: no Stage-10 module is imported by the solvers, the gate logic, or qta_full_sim.py
workspace-only: Stage-10 writers refuse to write into the repository root or any governed directory
no gate effect: automatic_gate_effect = NONE for every element; none may create or promote a gate
fail-closed optionality: an absent optional dependency reports UNAVAILABLE and defers to the in-repo authority
deterministic bytes: every Stage-10 artifact is reproducible byte-for-byte from the same inputs

elements.name: Python scientific core (NumPy / SciPy / QuTiP)
elements.boundary: the numerical authority of the project; every other stack element is additive to it

elements.name: Snakemake workflow
elements.boundary: wraps the authoritative commands; rewrites no solver and never writes the canonical tree

elements.name: uv (resolution and environment)
elements.boundary: Stage-10 optional packages are project extras, not dependency groups, so `uv sync --all-groups` stays lean

elements.name: Reproducible container
elements.boundary: the image fixes the software environment, not the host CPU: numerical bytes may differ between runners and are compared under the equivalence policy, never required equal. Built and run on a hosted runner on every push to the branch (qta-container-verify run 37966478474 at 5ab44a7, green): digest-pinned base confirmed against the served manifest, non-root user, no host virtualenv, the current harness and the generic end-to-end demonstration run in the image and compared with the same demonstration run natively. It certifies the runs it hosts, never a scientific result. The Rust extension is not built into it. Local builds in the development sandbox remain blocked by blob egress; the evidence is hosted.
elements.verification: bash container_verify.sh (inside the image); .github/workflows/container-verify.yml builds, runs and compares it on a hosted runner

elements.name: pytest + Hypothesis
elements.boundary: software verification only; a passing suite never converts a forecast into a measurement

elements.name: Ruff + mypy + Pydantic
elements.boundary: trusted-boundary validation only; the Pydantic models validate hand-editable documents (matrix update requests, this registry) and never become a competing vocabulary authority

elements.name: HDF5 data layer
elements.boundary: representation only; equivalence with the canonical CSV/JSON outputs is checked, not assumed

elements.name: RO-Crate packaging
elements.boundary: metadata packaging only; the crate restates the claim boundary and adds no evidence

elements.name: SLSA provenance + Sigstore signing
elements.boundary: a signature attests origin and integrity only, never scientific validity. What is adopted: the release candidate built deterministically for the commit (source archive, CycloneDX SBOM, SLSA-v1-layout provenance, index), signed with the workflow's GitHub OIDC identity, verified online and offline against the EXACT pinned identity and issuer, and a tamper suite run on a signed copy (supply-chain run 37966478453 at 5ab44a7, green). No SLSA build level is claimed: the provenance is produced by the workflow it describes, not by an isolated builder.
elements.verification: python tools/supply_chain.py verify --dir rc --mode online|offline|digests  # the hosted supply-chain job
open_items: no release is published and no tag is created: publication needs the owner's separate authorization
no SLSA build level is claimed

elements.name: Governed read-only retrieval over reviewed documents
elements.boundary: retrieval only — verbatim cited spans, no generation, no network, no model client; retrieved text is never evidence

elements.name: ParaView / VTK field export
elements.boundary: serializes solved cell-centred fields unchanged; no resampling, no smoothing, no added physics

elements.name: OpenUSD scene export
elements.optional_dependency: usd-core (extra: viz) — validation only; the .usda text is written directly
elements.boundary: geometric representation of the solved domain; no prim is a solver input

elements.name: SALib global sensitivity cross-check
elements.authority: qta_multiphysics/sensitivity_3d.py remains the sensitivity authority; qta_multiphysics/stack/sensitivity_salib.py is a cross-check
elements.boundary: disagreement with the canonical OAT ranking is reported, never resolved automatically
open_items: first cross-check disagrees with the canonical ranking on the top parameter (Kendall tau-b 0.667) — an open finding for human review, recorded in STACK.md

elements.name: OpenMDAO design-space exploration
elements.authority: qta_full_sim.py remains the operating-point authority; qta_multiphysics/stack/mdao_openmdao.py explores only
elements.boundary: only DESIGN-provenance parameters may be design variables; ASSUMED and LITERATURE_BOUND quantities are uncertainty and are rejected as knobs. Every result is NOT_A_RECOMMENDATION
elements.verification: snakemake --cores 1 s10_mdao_doe   # opt-in, one solve per sample

elements.name: FEniCSx (dolfinx) independent verifier
elements.authority: the governed producers in scientific/models remain the producers; FEniCSx is an INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION check whose verdict reaches authority only through the check contract and a distinct reviewer
elements.optional_dependency: dolfinx -- from the hash-pinned conda-forge lock integrations/fenicsx/environment.lock, created by tools/fenicsx_env.py; deliberately not a wheel dependency
elements.boundary: a verifier, never a producer: it admits or refuses a slab result and nothing it computes is admitted as a result. One problem class, the transient slab. Run single-process with MPI offered only self and shared-memory transports (D-2026-124). Executed on a hosted runner with the runtime REQUIRED (harness-integrations run 37966478567 at 5ab44a7: fenicsx and end-to-end jobs green). qta_multiphysics/stack/fem_fenicsx.py, the Stage-10 adapter for the legacy finite-volume backends, stays STAGED for that scope.
elements.verification: python tools/fenicsx_acceptance.py --out fenicsx_acceptance.json  # with QTA_FENICSX_PYTHON set; the hosted fenicsx and end-to-end jobs
open_items: one problem class only: no FEniCSx check exists for the 2D axisymmetric or the 3D thermal models, or for the legacy finite-volume backends

elements.name: Selective Rust kernels (PyO3)
elements.authority: the NumPy references in qta_multiphysics/stack/rust_kernel.py; a Rust kernel is an accelerator, never a second source of truth
elements.optional_dependency: qta_kernels — built on demand from rust/qta_kernels, never installed by default
elements.boundary: decided by measurement (docs/rust_kernel_decisions.json, re-derived by the hosted rust-kernels job, harness-integrations run 37966478567 at 5ab44a7): both kernels REJECTED -- face_conductance has no production call site; conductivity_power_law has parity that depends on the host's SIMD dispatch, no call site and a 0.61x workload speed. RUST_BACKEND_NOT_ACTIVE: NumPy is in force, and an explicit Rust selection is refused unless a committed decision is ADOPTED and its certificate applies to the process -- refused, never rerouted. The bit-parity admission mechanism stays in force for any later candidate. There is no active Rust scientific backend in this repository.
open_items: conductivity_power_law is REJECTED against a NumPy built with AVX-512 (2 ulp) and BIT-IDENTICAL against one without it: parity is conditional on the host's SIMD dispatch, which rust_kernel_status.json records beside every verdict. The decision does not depend on this host's verdict: it is REJECTED in every dispatch (no call site, 0.61x). D-2026-58
no scientific path consumes either kernel; a future candidate is decided by the same rule

elements.name: FMI 3.0 co-simulation (FMU runtime and boundary)
elements.authority: an FMU result is a SIMULATION_RESULT, NON_AUTHORITATIVE, admitted only through the independent check scientific/checks/fmu_rc2.py and a distinct reviewer
elements.optional_dependency: fmpy -- from the hash-pinned integrations/fmi/runtime.lock, in its own runtime (tools/isolated_runtime.py)
elements.boundary: one generic FMU (integrations/fmi/thermal_rc2, a two-node thermal RC network) is built from C against hash-checked FMI 3.0 headers, loaded by fmpy, stepped, its state serialized, restored and replayed; P2-P5 hold for it; its fault twin is REJECTED by the independent check. Executed on a hosted runner (harness-integrations run 37966478567 at 5ab44a7: fmi and end-to-end jobs green). Its bytes are claimed identical between two builds on one host only. qta_multiphysics/stack/fmi_contract.py keeps its DEFERRED interface contract for exporting the legacy solvers, which is not done.
elements.verification: python tools/fmi_acceptance.py  # with QTA_FMI_PYTHON set; the hosted fmi and end-to-end jobs
open_items: no FMU of the legacy finite-volume solvers is exported: fmi_contract.py's prerequisites for that export (FMI-P1 to FMI-P5) stay open for those solvers

elements.boundary: decides admission of results and computes none: no scientific module imports it (tests/test_agent_substrate_isolation.py), and nothing learned or proposed reaches VERIFIED except through a governed run, an independent check and a distinct reviewer
elements.verification: python -m pytest tests/test_agent_*.py  # and the qta-agent-substrate workflow's mutation shards

elements.authority: scientific: models produce ResultBundles, checks return VerificationResults, the authority store admits
elements.boundary: imports no hardware ontology and no legacy QTA module (tests/test_scientific_import_isolation.py); an HDF5 bundle is a representation, never evidence of admission

elements.authority: qta_agent/authority.py: a proposal is NON_AUTHORITATIVE data; only a governed run, an independent check and a distinct reviewer reach a decision
